newsitem.title: ITALY: Fresh snag hits Priebke war crimes trial in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Fresh snag hits Priebke war crimes trial in Italy.

text.p: Military court authorities in Italy have decided they are not competent to try former SS captain Erich Priebke for alleged war crimes and have passed the case to civil jurisdiction, judicial officials said on Thursday.

Military prosecutor Antonino Intelisano told Reuters that civil authorities would now have to decide whether to try Priebke, who has been held in detention for more than a year for his alleged role in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity.
Priebke was extradited from Argentina in November 1995 to stand trial for involvement in the 1944 massacre by the SS of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves south of Rome.
A first trial in a military court ended in uproar in August when the bench found Priebke guilty of complicity in murder but ruled that he was no longer liable to punishment.
The verdict was later overturned by higher court judges and a new military trial ordered in a case that has been shrouded in legal complexity and confusion since it began.

Intelisano, who said he did not agree with the latest ruling, said Italy's highest court, the Court of Cassation, may eventually have to decide which branch of the judiciary, civil or military, was competent in the case.
